title: Embracing the future of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom: the relevance of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking in modern education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how AI should be integrated into education in ways that improve learning while avoiding overreliance, plagiarism, hallucinations, and other risks. Rather than evaluating a specific classroom intervention with outcome measures, it presents a conceptual discussion grounded in the author’s teaching experience at Kalaidos University of Applied Sciences in Zurich, Switzerland, together with informal discussions with students and staff and a narrative literature review.

The paper argues that effective educational use of AI rests on three core competencies: AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking. It describes a university-level policy response (“AI guidelines”) that allows generative AI use in academic work, but requires transparency about which model was used, how it was used, how outputs were critically evaluated, and where in the manuscript AI contributed. The author also provides practical examples of classroom uses such as student AI experiments, AI-generated case studies, AI-supported curriculum design, gamification, and immersive technologies.

The population and context are primarily higher-education students and educators at a Swiss university of applied sciences, though the author notes the ideas may also be useful for children and K-12 settings. The main conclusion is that banning or fully unrestricted use of AI are both problematic; instead, institutions should build a culture of responsible AI use through guidelines, workshops, ongoing staff support, explicit curriculum integration, and instruction in prompting and critical evaluation. The paper emphasizes that AI is most useful when treated as a sparring partner that can generate ideas and suggestions, but whose outputs must be checked against evidence and not copied verbatim.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual discussion and narrative literature review rather than an empirical evaluation of a specific AI intervention in K-12. It does not report a controlled study, quantitative outcomes, or a reproducible methodology for impact estimation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper proposes general guidance, workflows, and institutional recommendations for AI literacy and prompt engineering, but it does not measure learner or teacher outcomes. As a result, there is no demonstrated impact size to classify beyond theoretical or practical suggestions.
